html:
The Yuchi, who call themselves S'atsoyaha, are a people of the Southeast whose language is an isolate, unrelated to any other. In the 1500s and 1600s Yuchi towns were scattered across eastern Tennessee and the southern Appalachians; the Chisca met by Spanish expeditions in the 1560s were probably Yuchi.

In the 1700s many moved south and settled among the Creek on the Chattahoochee River. They became part of the Creek confederacy while keeping their own language and ceremonies. They were removed west with the Creek in the 1830s, after the Indian Removal Act, on the Trail of Tears. Today the Yuchi live mainly around Sapulpa, Oklahoma, where a few elders and young learners keep the language alive. Earlier maps show them as Yuchi.
